# Robust window regeneration with causal quantum detectors

29 October 2026, Australia/Brisbane. Authored extension by compact_memory.
Independent review is separate. Builds on OUTPUT_PORT_REGENERATION.md and
the accepted predecessor first-mean/contact machinery at their stated scope.

## 1. Goal, physical scope and statement

Exact full swaps are not needed for a polylogarithmic finite-memory
representation when a finite-mean invariant region is available. Work with
one retained canonical oscillator a and a finite sequence of fresh modes
b_j. Fresh b_j have fixed thermal means n_j<=nbar, are independent of the
whole incoming state and one another, and can equivalently be supplied as
a finite product before the window with access delayed until their contact.
Thermal means may differ with j but are not selected from a quantum record
inside the window. Such a selection would require its own construction.

Each prescribed passive contact couples only a to its own b_j. At the end
its retained amplitude is c_j, with |c_j|<=cbar<1. Scalar waveforms and any
passive phases are supplied and fixed independently of incoming records.
During the contact, source-controlled bounded Weyl vertices have total
variation action <=alpha and one-particle displacement norm <=b. Full sines
and cosines in either canonical quadrature are examples. No nonlinearity
is linearized. Source/data/controller operations act on neither a nor the
currently interacting b_j nor future fresh modes. After departure b_j may
undergo arbitrary common complete causal detection or joint processing
with past departed modes and source/controller, with actual records used
for source feedback. It cannot return to the passive network. Its quantum
state may remain as detector memory; that extra memory is not compacted.

Assume the exact complete dynamics has a uniform boundary contract
Tr[N_a rho]<=E. The accepted first-row construction supplies such a
contract, for example P=sqrt(E),

    sqrt(cbar^2 P^2+nbar)+alpha*b <= P.                 (1)

Common complete operations on departed modes preserve the unconditional
mean of a. Normalized rare conditional branches need not obey (1).

For an L-contact window ending at any cut, define

    delta_L=asin(cbar^L)*sqrt((2*nbar+1)*E+nbar),
    T_window(d,L)=delta_L+T_d(alpha*L,b,nbar),           (2)

where T_d is any of the explicit certificates in

29 October 2026, Australia/Brisbane. Root construction. Draft pending actual
independent review. Predecessor proofs and reviews are not modified.

## Objective and scope

The output-port tail theorem in `../compact/` is useful only if the resulting
finite memory can be evolved by a finite, completely positive instrument.
This note constructs that bridge. It does not identify unknown parameters,
make an unknown initial state computable, or promise classical simulation
of a source register whose dimension grows exponentially with its qubits.

source/controller/reference K, prescribed passive quadratic evolution that
preserves N=N_a+N_b, and a bounded interaction

    V(t)=sum_l B_l(t) tensor W(f_l(t)),
    sum_l ||B_l(t)|| <= a(t),  A=integral a(t),
    ||f_l(t)|| <= kappa.

The sum may be a finite-variation integral; V is self-adjoint. The Weyl
convention is W(f)=exp(i(a(f)+a(f)^dagger)). For a sine vertex, the two
Weyl coefficients have total variation equal to the source amplitude.
Several conjugate quadrature vertices are permitted; kappa bounds their
full two-mode feature norm. Put source-only controls in their common
interaction picture, or insert their complete isometries at their real
times. These preserve all number projections used below.

The finite contact input has a supported on 0,...,d-1, potentially
entangled with K and a reference. Fresh b is independent thermal with
mean n. Parameter uncertainty, preparation error, detector uncertainty and
physical errors are separate from the mathematical approximation here.

# A fully enclosed prediction for the concurrent quantum contact

29 October 2026, Australia/Brisbane. Author: fault_locality. This is a
validated numerical action construction. Independent review is separate;
the word certified refers to the analytic enclosures described here.

## 1. Completed result

For the exact infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian

    H=(pi/2) i(b^dagger a-a^dagger b)
        +(1/8) sigma_x sin[(a+a^dagger)/2]
        +(1/8) sigma_y sin[i(a^dagger-a)/2],              (1)

acting for time one, with source I/2 and both oscillators in vacuum, the
executed calculation encloses the exact source expectation in

    0.009748778824845387583321769614292341
       <= <sigma_z> <=
    0.009748846972041638565154374216800806.              (2)

The two full sine terms are on throughout the passive contact. This is an
infinite-model prediction, not a floating-point cutoff comparison. The
finite numerical contribution to the Z allowance is below 6.32e-34; the
roughly 3.41e-8 half-width is dominated by the explicit infinite-to-finite
Galerkin bound. No statistical samples or measured parameters are used.

Equation (2) certifies the nonunital source operation: a classical mixture
of initially independent Hamiltonian trajectories would preserve I/2.
It gives no hardware performance or logical computing advantage claim.
The input, controls and Hamiltonian in (1) are stipulated mathematical
resources. Physical calibration, delivery, losses and readout uncertainty
remain separate ledgers.

## 2. Finite restriction with an infinite-model allowance

Let P project onto total oscillator number N_a+N_b<M, with M=24. The
source tensor this space has dimension

    D=2*M*(M+1)/2=600.

The matrix H_M is the EXACT restriction P H P, not a matrix sine of a
truncated quadrature. The passive term commutes with total number.

The bounded interaction has total Weyl variation action A=1/4 and each
